# Support ticket #4163 — "Our revocation callbacks never arrive"

**Reporter:** Priya S., Partner Success (escalated by a newly onboarded member league) · **Severity:**
high — every revocation since they went live; one customer affected, and it is the largest account
we have onboarded.

> Our webhook health check is green, but a customer we onboarded — one with a lot of settings —
> says their revocation callbacks never arrive. Other customers are fine. Same code, same steps.
> Their door systems keep admitting members whose credentials the league has already revoked,
> until the next scheduled status-list refresh. Nobody on the team can make it happen on their own
> machine, and the test suite is green.

**What support has confirmed:** when a customer revokes a credential, every relying party that has
subscribed to that customer's status changes is told, whatever the size of the customer's account
and however any one relying party's endpoint is behaving. A green health check means callbacks are
reaching customers.

**Your job:** get revocation callbacks arriving for every customer's subscribers — not just the
account that complained.
On branch master
nothing to commit, working tree clean

content.text:
I've fixed ticket #4163. Revocation callbacks now reach every subscriber, including those of large accounts, and the health check no longer reports green when they don't. The full backend suite passes: 75 tests, 0 build warnings (clippy isn't installed here, so it wasn't run). Nothing is committed yet.

## Why it only hit the big customer
The runtime kills each notifier run after a hard 10 seconds (`reference/infra/webhook-config.yaml`), and three bugs in `backend/src/notifier.rs` combined against that limit:

1. **Reading the settings got slower with every setting.** To find a tenant's webhooks, the notifier read *all* of its settings, 100 per page at 50 ms a page. A customer with around 20,000 settings uses up the whole 10 s just on that read. The runtime then stops the run, and none of that customer's subscribers is called. Small tenants need one page, which is why nobody could reproduce it.
2. **Subscribers were called one after another, with no per-call timeout.** One endpoint that hung or was slow held up everyone queued behind it. Also, the internal 10 s timeout was the same length as the runtime's limit, so it never got the chance to fire. The README says failed deliveries are retried, but no retry code existed.
3. **The health check measured something else.** It only looked at a "canary" at `https://example.com/webhooks/status`, which is called *before* any customer subscriber. That's a reserved documentation domain, which `reference/infra/reserved-domains.md` forbids as a health target. In tests, a built-in fake answered it with a 200. So the check was green whatever happened to customers' callbacks.

## What changed
- **Finding webhooks:** the notifier now uses the existing `tenant-kind` index, so the cost depends on how many webhooks a tenant has, not how many settings.
- **Calling subscribers:** all subscribers are called at the same time. Each call has a 3 s timeout, and failures that might be temporary (network errors, timeouts, HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx) are retried up to 3 times with increasing waits. Everything has to finish within 8 s, leaving time before the runtime's 10 s cutoff. Each subscription still gets exactly one recorded outcome.
- **Health check:** I removed the `example.com` canary and its fake response in `backend/src/webhook.rs`. `canary_healthy()` is now `healthy()`, which is true only when the most recent revocation reached *every* one of its subscribers. I updated `backend/README.md` to match.
- **Tests:** I added 7 tests to `backend/tests/notifier.rs`, covering a large tenant, a hanging endpoint, slow endpoints, retry after a temporary failure, the budget ending before the runtime limit, the health check going red, and no calls to reserved domains. All 7 failed on the old code and pass now.

## Decisions for you
- **Health check strictness:** under the new rule, one subscriber whose endpoint is permanently down turns the check red whenever that tenant revokes something. That matches what support believes a green check means. If you'd rather it only go red when the notifier itself fails, it's a small change.
- **Platform follow-ups (not in this repo):** the notifier's deploy config has `alarms: []` and no platform-level retries, so nothing alerts when deliveries fail. If you want an end-to-end canary back, it needs an endpoint that the platform itself runs, which Platform Infrastructure would have to provide.
- **Subscriber concurrency:** all of a tenant's subscribers are called at once with no upper limit. That's fine for the numbers we see today. If a tenant ever has thousands of webhooks, it would be worth adding a cap.
